articles.title: Carbon 2×2 Twill
articles.summary: Diagonal ±45° twill weave with over-2/under-2 interlace; sharp metallic peaks at tow crowns, tight micro grain. A smooth satin sheen with a faint directional grain; true twill diagonals only appear when the weave is seen on a larger or closer crop.
articles.what: Standard 2×2 twill carbon fiber — diagonal ±45° tow families, over-2/under-2 interlace, sharp metallic peaks at tow crowns Up close: Extremely fine near-vertical streaking, hairline ticks about 3-5 px apart, with a hint of diagonal ticks in the dark floor area. The twill weave itself is too fine to resolve; you see a delicate directional grain inside the highlight. From a distance: A smooth satin sheen with a faint directional grain; true twill diagonals only appear when the weave is seen on a larger or closer crop. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Carbon & Composite Weave (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Carbon & Composite Weave", or search for "Carbon 2×2 Twill".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, splitter and spoiler where carbon is expected
Best over black or dark metallic paint
Numbers stay clear; the weave is hairline.
Almost nothing: a whisper of vertical grain
Pairs well with: gloss, matte, metallic, chrome.
pitfalls: Not a black weave paint: no colour, only shine grain
Not Carbon Weave or Forged carbon: this is the fine standard twill, quieter than a bold checker
Avoid: reads flat at distance, fights busy graphics.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.goal: Layer Carbon 2×2 Twill over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.
